questions.question: What is the difference (in Rs.) between the compound interest, when interest is compounded 6-monthly, and the simple interest on a sum of Rs. 20,000 for 1(1)/(2) year at 10% p.a.?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principal = Rs. 20,000

Rate = 10%

Time = 1(1)/(2) years = 3/2 years​​​​

**Formula used:**

A = P (1 + r/100)t

SI = (P × R × T)/100

**Calculation:**

If Interest is compounded 6-monthly, then

Rate = 10/2 = 5%

Time = 3/2 × 2 = 3 years

Now,

Amount = 20,000 × (1 + 5/100)³

⇒ (20,000 × 21/20 × 21/20 × 21/20)

⇒ Rs. 23,152.5

CI = (23,152.5 – 20,000)

⇒ Rs. 3,152.5

SI = (P × R × T)/100

⇒ [(20,000 × 10 × 3/2) × 100]

⇒ Rs. 3000

Required difference = (3152.5 – 3000)

⇒ 152.5

**∴ The required difference is 152.5 **

questions.question: A sum of money becomes two times of itself in 8 years at simple interest, and it becomes four times of itself in 2 years at compound interest, when interest is compounded annually. Find the ratio of the rate of simple interest to the rate of compound interest offered per year.
questions.solution:
Given:

A sum of money becomes two times of itself in 8 years at simple interest, and it becomes four times of itself in 2 years at compound interest, when interest is compounded annually.

Concept used:

1. Simple Interest, SI = (P × R × T)/100

Amount = P + SI

where

P = Principal amount

R = Rate of interest per year

T = Time in years

2. In case of the compound interest,

Amount = P(1 + R/100)N

CI = P(1 + R/100)N - P

where

P = Principal amount

R = Rate of interest per year

N = Time in years

Calculation:

Let the principal amount, simple rate of interest and compound rate of interest be P, R, and r respectively.

According to the concept,

P + (P × R × 8)/100 = 2P

⇒ (P × R × 8)/100 = P

⇒ R = 100/8

⇒ R = 12.5

According to the concept,

P(1 + r/100)² = 4P

⇒ (1 + r/100)2 = 4

⇒ (1 + r/100) = 2

⇒ r/100 = 1

⇒ r = 100

Now, the ratio of the rate of simple interest to the rate of compound interest offered per year

⇒ 12.5 : 100

⇒ 1 : 8

**∴ The ratio of the rate of simple interest to the rate of compound interest offered per year is 1 : 8.**

questions.question: What is the compound interest on Rs. 8400 for 2 years at 10% per annum compounded annually?
questions.solution:
**Given:- **

Principal amount(P) = 8400 

Time = 2 year 

Rate % = 10%

**Formula used:- **

Compound Interest = P ( 1 + R/100 )T - P

where T = time and P = principal R = Rate of interest 

**Calculation:- **

Compound Interest = 8400 ( 1 + 10/100)² - 8400 

⇒ 8400 (110/100)² - 8400 

⇒ 10164 - 8400 = 1764** 

 ∴ The required answer is__ 1764__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__**

R% = 1/10 

P = 10

A = 10 + 1 =11 

⇒ Principle → Amount 

 

⇒ 10 → 11

For 2 years

⇒ (10)² → (11)² 

⇒ 100 → 121 

So, CI = 121 - 100 = 21

Comparing the real data 

 ⇒ CI = (21/100) × 8400 =1764

questions.question: Find compound interest on Rs. 8000 at 15% per annum for 2 years, compounded annually.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principal (P) = Rs. 8000

Rate of interest (R) = 15% per annum

Time (T) = 2 years

**Formula:**

Compound Interest = P(1 + R/100)² - P

**Calculation:**

⇒ Compound Interest = 8000(1 + 15/100)² - 8000

⇒ Compound Interest = 8000(1.15)² - 8000

Compound Interest = Rs. 2580

**Therefore, the compound interest on Rs. 8000 at 15% per annum for 2 years, compounded annually, is Rs. 2580.**

questions.question: The compound interest received on Rs. 18,000 for 2 years is Rs. 7,920, when the interest is compounded annually. What is the rate of interest per annum?
questions.solution:
Given:

The compound interest accrued on Rs. 18000 in two years is Rs. 7920.

Formula Used:

C.I = Principal × ((1 + r/100)t - 1);

Calculation:

⇒ 7920 = 18000 × ((1 + r/100)2 - 1)

⇒ 7920/18000 = ((1 + r/100)2 - 1)

⇒ 11/25 + 1 = (1 + r/100)2

⇒ 36/25 = (1 + r/100)²

Take root both sides

⇒ 6/5 = (1 + r/100)

⇒ r/100 = 1/5

⇒ r = 20

∴ required rate of interest = 20%

**∴ Option 3 is the correct answer.**
